display.title: Sefiras HaOmer: Making Every Day Count (Zalman and the Lost Nickel)
display.summary_short: Counting the Omer teaches that time is precious. Uncle Yossi explains with the story of Zalman, who learned to stop mourning a lost nickel and guard the coins he still had.
display.summary_long: A Sefirah teaching from the Tzivos Hashem radio show. Since the second night of Pesach we count the 49 days of the Omer, and one lesson is to count time itself. Time marches on: we cannot stop it, speed it up or slow it down, but we can control what fills it, using each day wisely instead of wasting it. A day without accomplishment is lost and can never come back. Uncle Yossi tells of little Zalman, whose nickel slipped through a hole in his pocket. His father gives him another, and then another, but Zalman keeps returning to say how much more he would have with the first nickel, until his father explains that he must forget the lost coin and take care of the ones he has. So too, we make every day worth counting by davening carefully, learning Torah and doing mitzvos, thanking Hashem for the gift of time, and He will lengthen our days in good health and happiness.
display.lesson: Time is a precious gift from Hashem: don't dwell on lost days, but fill each new day with davening, Torah and mitzvos.
